questions.q: In the one-hot demo, what is the cosine similarity between "car" and "automobile"?
options: 1.0, because they are synonyms
0.5, because they are related
-1.0, because they are different words
0.0, exactly the same as "car" versus "banana"
questions.explain: One-hot vectors for different words are orthogonal, so every pair of distinct words has cosine 0 and no meaning is captured.

options: A dense vector of numbers representing an item so that similar items are close together
A compressed copy of the original text file
A list of the most frequent words in a document
A model's training loss value
questions.explain: An embedding maps text (or other data) to a vector whose geometry reflects similarity.

questions.q: Why is cosine similarity commonly used to compare embeddings?
options: It only works for vectors with exactly three dimensions
It measures the angle between vectors, comparing direction rather than length
It always returns integers between 0 and 10
It requires no vectors at all
questions.explain: Cosine is the cosine of the angle between two vectors: 1 for the same direction, near 0 for unrelated, negative for opposite.

questions.q: Tickets "charge on my card was wrong" and "please refund the payment" share no words. What did the demo show?
options: TF-IDF cosine was about 1.0 and SVD cosine was 0.0
Both representations gave a cosine of 0.0
TF-IDF cosine was 0.0, while the 3-dimensional SVD embedding gave about 1.0
Both representations gave a cosine of about 1.0
questions.explain: TF-IDF sees no overlap. The SVD embedding groups words that appear in similar tickets, so the two tickets land close together.

questions.q: Which rule matters when using embeddings for search?
options: Use a different embedding model for queries than for documents to add variety
Vectors from any two models can be compared directly
Only compare vectors produced by the same model, and embed queries with the model used for the documents
Always normalize vectors to length 100
questions.explain: Different models produce vectors in different spaces, so cross-model comparisons are meaningless.
